lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Complete a table for rule “×2 then +1”: inputs 1,2,3,4.

FEEDBACK
Outputs 3,5,7,9.

WATCH FOR
Filling a table without checking the same rule for every row breaks the pattern.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Build eight input–output tables from stated rules and invent rules for four completed tables. Predict the 10th term for three.

Write a short reflection naming one step you corrected and why.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Pattern of squares: position 1→3, 2→5, 3→7 (odd numbers). Table columns help see +2 each time. Rule: output = 2×input + 1.

TRY FIRST
Complete a table for rule “×2 then +1”: inputs 1,2,3,4.

FEEDBACK
Outputs 3,5,7,9.
teach_steps.explain:
Growing patterns can be recorded in tables relating position (input) to term value (output) so the rule is visible.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner choose methods based on place value, quantity and accurate working, rather than guessing digits by shape alone. Keep every step justified.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the places, values or distances that carry the method. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your working with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your reasoning? If a digit or place is uncertain, identify what would have to be regrouped or counted again. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
teach_steps.notice: Filling a table without checking the same rule for every row breaks the pattern. Correct the value or method, not just the appearance of the digits.
